headline: AI rebound and firm US data lift the dollar to a two-week high; euro sinks, peso breaks 64
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.3% to near 102.3–102.4, its highest since mid-October, as an AI-led stock rebound drained haven demand from the yen and franc and beats on durable goods and consumer confidence kept a December Fed hike in view before Wednesday's expected hold. The euro was the weakest major, down about 0.4% to 1.1126 on French gloom, while the Aussie and Taiwan dollar gained and the peso closed past 64 for the first time.
drivers: Risk-on and US data firm the dollar

Anthropic's IPO filing and Meta's equity plan revived the AI trade, so the yen and franc lost their haven bid; USD/JPY rose about 0.2% to 157.83 and USD/CHF to 0.8292. September durable goods rose 1.8% and Conference Board confidence jumped 7.5 points to 91.7, and futures still price about 80% odds of a December Fed hike.
France and the ECB weigh on the euro

French household confidence fell to a 13-year low and the 10-year OAT yield rose about 4bp to near 4.96%, while the ECB lending survey showed its hikes biting. EUR/USD fell about 0.4% to 1.1126, its weakest in about two weeks and down about 1.7% in October.
Oil eases, but importers still slide

Brent fell about 1.7% to settle near $113.9 as Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani envoys talked with Tehran, which hurt the loonie (USD/CAD 1.4051). Yet the peso closed at a record 64.17 and the rupiah near 18,145, 25 points from its record, as fuel bills and outflows outweighed cheaper crude.
view: Mildly firmer over the next 1–2 weeks: US data keep beating, a December hike is mostly but not fully priced, and Europe's fiscal stress caps the euro. I back the dollar against the euro and the rupiah and peso, but fade it against the yen and loonie, where the BoJ and BoC are turning hawkish and Tokyo is warning. A dovish Fed hold on Wednesday or a DXY close below 101.70 would turn me neutral; a Fed that firmly signals December and a DXY close above 102.80 would make me dollar-positive across the board.
ideas: Short from 157.50–157.80 (filled) into Friday's BoJ and Tokyo's warnings, for 155.00, stop 158.60, about 3:1.
Short from 1.4030–1.4050 (filled) on an expected BoC hike against a Fed hold, for 1.3880, stop 1.4130, about 2:1.
Long: add on dips to 18,080–18,100 near record lows as outflows and MSCI risk persist, for 18,300, stop 18,040, about 4:1.
review: USD/PHP's long from 63.50 is about 1% in favour (64.20 high, 64.30 target missed by 10 centavos), USD/IDR's about 0.8% and USD/TWD's fade from 32.53 about 0.3%; USD/JPY and USD/CAD shorts are about 0.1–0.2% against and USD/CHF's 0.4% against; EUR/USD, USD/CNH, USD/KRW and EUR/JPY entries were missed as moves ran our way. I cut the franc short to a range, turn AUD/USD up on hot CPI, lower the euro and EUR/JPY entries and trail the peso and rupiah stops.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.4% to 1.1126, a two-week low and the weakest major; ECB fixing 1.1150.
eurusd.why: The euro did most of the moving. French household confidence fell to a 13-year low and OAT yields rose about 4bp to near 4.96% after Monday's Moody's relief faded, and the ECB's lending survey showed its hikes are already tightening credit, which trims the case for more. A firmer dollar on strong US durable goods and confidence data added to the drop through 1.1150 support.
eurusd.outlook: Bearish: I lower the sell zone to 1.1160–1.1180, since rallies fail earlier, and target 1.1050. A close above 1.1240 ends the call; a hawkish ECB on Oct 29 or a dovish Fed are the risks.
eurusd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), the ECB (Oct 29), euro-area flash CPI (Oct 30) and French spreads.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.25% to 1.3307, at the range floor, but near a 17-month high against the euro before the Budget.

view.call: 1.3280–1.3450; buy dips, Budget is the swing factor.

gbpusd.why: The dollar did the moving. Sterling fell with the euro and yen as the dollar index rose to two-week highs, but it held near 83.7 pence per euro, close to its strongest since May 2025, as traders expect a largely undramatic Budget from Chancellor Healey on Wednesday. Overnight euro-sterling implied volatility of about 5.3% shows far less anxiety than before last year's Budget.
gbpusd.outlook: Range 1.3280–1.3450, buying near the bottom: a bond-friendly Budget and BoE hike pricing support sterling. A gilt selloff that closes cable below 1.3280 turns me bearish; above 1.3450 turns me bullish.
gbpusd.watch: The Budget and the Fed (Oct 28), then the BoE (Nov 5).

audusd.note: Up about 0.4% to 0.7045 against the dollar trend, then near 0.7053 after a hot Q3 CPI.

view.call: Buy 0.7000–0.7020; hot CPI, RBA hike odds.

audusd.why: The Aussie did the moving. China's industrial profits jumped 14.4% y/y in September, the AI rally lifted risk appetite and markets priced about two-thirds odds of an RBA hike on Nov 3 before the CPI. Right after the session, Q3 headline CPI rose 1.3% q/q against 1.2% expected and the annual trimmed mean hit 3.7% against 3.6%, well above the RBA's 0.8% quarterly path.
audusd.outlook: I turn bullish: the CPI makes a Nov 3 hike to 4.85% likely, so I buy dips to 0.7000–0.7020 for 0.7130. A close below 0.6950, likely on a hawkish Fed or an RBA hold, ends the call.
audusd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), China PMIs (Oct 31) and the RBA (Nov 3).

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.2% to 157.83 as the yen lost its haven bid; failed again near 158.
usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving. The AI-led stock rebound erased more of last week's haven gains and the BoJ is expected to hold at 1.25% on Friday, so the dollar edged up to about 157.9. Finance Minister Katayama said Tokyo is ready to take decisive action in the currency market, which gave the yen only a brief lift but kept buyers away from 158.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the short from 157.50–157.80, about 0.2% against me, for 155.00: the BoJ is likely to flag upside inflation risks and keep a December hike in play, and intervention risk caps the pair. A close above 158.60 ends the call.
usdjpy.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), US GDP and PCE (Oct 29), the BoJ outlook report (Oct 30) and Tokyo's 159–160 line.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.2% to 0.8292, a third straight gain; tested 0.8295 resistance.
usdchf.why: The franc did most of the moving. The AI-led rebound in stocks cut demand for havens, and SNB minutes said rate gaps make the franc an attractive funding currency, while the dollar firmed on strong US data. A fall in Swiss 10-year yields to near 0.47% on European fiscal worries limited the move.
usdchf.outlook: I cut the short from 0.8240–0.8260, about 0.4% against me, because the haven case has weakened with stocks; I now see a 0.8230–0.8330 range. A close above 0.8330 opens 0.8400; a fresh stock selloff would send it back to 0.8230.
usdchf.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), risk sentiment, European spreads and Swiss CPI (early Nov).

usdcad.note: Up about 0.3% to 1.4051 as oil fell, a third day off Friday's 1.3966 five-week low.

view.call: Short from 1.4030–1.4050; BoC hike vs Fed hold.

usdcad.why: Oil and position-squaring moved it. WTI fell about 1.8% to just under $100 as Iran diplomacy advanced, and traders took profit on the loonie's recent rally before the BoC, which markets see about 75–80% likely to hike to 2.50% on Wednesday. The US–Canada two-year yield gap has narrowed to about 1.36 points from 1.62 on Oct 9.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the short from 1.4030–1.4050, about 0.1% against me, for 1.3880: a hike alongside a Fed hold narrows the rate gap further. A close above 1.4130, likely on a BoC hold or a dovish hike, ends the call.
usdcad.watch: The BoC rate decision and MPR and the Fed (Oct 28), oil, and US tariffs due Oct 30.

usdcnh.note: Steady near 6.665, close to four-year yuan highs; fixing 6.7171, 440 pips weaker than estimates.

view.call: Sell 6.670–6.680; PBOC lets the yuan grind up.

usdcnh.why: The PBOC set the pace. Tuesday's 6.7171 midpoint was slightly weaker than Monday's and 440 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate, a clear signal it wants slower gains. Exporter conversion and a 14.4% jump in September industrial profits kept the yuan firm anyway, so it held near 6.668 onshore while the dollar rose elsewhere.
usdcnh.outlook: A managed grind lower: I lower the sell zone to 6.670–6.680 for 6.630. Fixings closer to estimates would speed it up; a close above 6.705 or a sharp China stock selloff ends the call.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China PMIs (Oct 31), US–China headlines and the Fed (Oct 28).

usdhkd.note: Flat near 7.8455, still pinned near the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdhkd.why: Rate gaps keep it there. HIBOR stays well below US rates, which sit near 4% on the Fed's 3.75–4.00% range, so borrowing Hong Kong dollars to hold US dollars still pays. DBS expects the HKMA to keep defending 7.85 and HIBOR to drift higher into year-end, but there was no fresh intervention on Tuesday.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in the 7.83–7.85 band. A test of 7.85 would force HKMA buying and lift HIBOR; a dovish Fed would pull it off the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), HIBOR and HKMA action at 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Little changed near 1.2810, just below 100-day average resistance at 1.2820.
usdsgd.why: The broad dollar and yuan set the tone. The Singapore dollar held up better than the euro and yen as the yuan stayed near four-year highs, but the dollar's two-week high kept the pair near the top of its range. OCBC notes the S$NEER sits in the upper half of the MAS band, which limits how much the currency can outperform.
usdsgd.outlook: Range 1.2720–1.2830: soft local data and a strong S$NEER balance out. A close above 1.2830 would open 1.2900; below 1.2720 reopens downside.
usdsgd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), Singapore jobs data and the yuan.

usdkrw.note: Won eased 0.6 to 1,323.7 at the Seoul close, near its 2026 best; 1-month NDF later 1,326.4.
usdkrw.why: Flows and data supported the won, but caution capped it. Q3 GDP grew 1.0% q/q, triple the BoK's August projection of 0.3%, chip exporters kept selling dollars into month-end and foreigners bought about 593 billion won of shares as the Kospi jumped over 3%. Importer dollar buying near the year low and caution before the Fed held it in the low 1,320s, and the NDF drifted up as the dollar firmed overnight.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep selling rallies into 1,330–1,335 for 1,310: exporter supply and growth momentum favour the won. A close above 1,345 ends the call; heavy foreign stock selling is the risk.
usdkrw.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), Samsung and SK hynix results, Korea's October exports (Nov 1) and month-end flows.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar rose 5.6 cents to 32.452 on reopening, the day's best, after a 32.604 low.
usdtwd.why: Taiwan's own flows did the moving. After a four-day break, it first weakened toward 32.60 on pending foreign outflows, then rallied to close at the day's high as the AI rebound lifted chip stocks and exporters sold dollars. The central bank's report to lawmakers showed $54.3 billion of net foreign outflows since July, a reminder of why it leans against weakness near 32.50 and above.
usdtwd.outlook: My fade filled near 32.53 and is about 0.3% in favour; I hold for 32.10. A close above 32.80, likely on renewed foreign Taiex selling, would stop it.
usdtwd.watch: The central bank at the legislature (Oct 28), foreign Taiex flows, US big-tech earnings and the Fed (Oct 28).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0865/0900 at the 6pm close from 4.0855/0895, but firmed on most other currencies.
usdmyr.why: Caution before the Fed. The ringgit opened firmer on resilient Malaysian fundamentals and Iran diplomacy, then slipped slightly as the dollar index climbed toward two-week highs. It still gained against the Singapore dollar, rupiah and most majors, holding up far better than oil-importing neighbours.
usdmyr.outlook: Range-bound around 4.07–4.10. Bank Negara and exports support it, but it rarely moves far without the broad dollar.
usdmyr.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), oil and Bank Negara (Nov 5).

usdphp.note: Peso fell 22 centavos to a record-low close of 64.17, its first finish past 64; low 64.20.

view.call: Long; add 63.95–64.05. Oil, BoP gap swamp BSP hikes.

usdphp.why: Confidence and the balance of payments, not rates, are driving it. Even with Brent easing, fuel import costs, a widening payments gap and expectations of a hawkish Fed kept dollar demand heavy, and volume rose to $1.7 billion. Economists note last week's surprise 50bp BSP hike to 5.50% has not stopped the slide, the peso's ninth record low in October.
usdphp.outlook: My long from 63.50 is about 1% in favour; I raise the target to 64.50 and trail the stop to 63.80, adding on dips to 63.95–64.05. An Iran deal or heavy BSP dollar sales that close it below 63.80 end the call.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments and possible off-cycle action, oil and Iran, the Fed (Oct 28) and US midterms (Nov 3).

usdidr.note: Rupiah fell about 0.2% to near 18,145 (Refinitiv), 25 points from its record; JISDOR 18,139.
usdidr.why: Domestic worries outweighed cheaper oil. The Jakarta index fell about 2% as foreign investors kept selling on MSCI's market-status review and fiscal strain from the energy subsidy bill, while the current-account gap near 3.3% of GDP leaves the rupiah exposed. Bank Indonesia's presence slowed but did not stop the drift toward June's record close of about 18,170.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long from near 18,000, about 0.8% in favour, adding on dips to 18,080–18,100 for 18,300 and trailing the stop to 18,040. A credible MSCI fix or heavy BI intervention that closes it below 18,040 ends the call.
usdidr.watch: MSCI's review, Jakarta foreign flows, BI action at the record, oil and the Fed (Oct 28).

usdinr.note: Rupee rose 3 paise to about 95.12 in a tight 95.09–95.24 range on likely RBI support.

view.call: 94.50–95.50; RBI near the top, oil caps the rupee.

usdinr.why: The RBI steadied it. Dealers saw likely central bank dollar sales after three days of losses totalling 77 paise, while cheaper crude and hopes for US–Iran diplomacy helped. A firm dollar, weak local stocks and importer demand stopped the rupee from recovering more.
usdinr.outlook: Range 94.50–95.50: the RBI defends the top, while oil above $110 blocks a big rupee rally. A close above 95.50 would signal a new weaker leg; below 94.50 extends the RBI-led recovery.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran headlines, RBI action, foreign flows and the Fed (Oct 28).

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.2% to near 175.60 as the euro fell harder than the yen.
eurjpy.why: The euro was the weaker leg. Both fell against the dollar, but French confidence at a 13-year low, rising OAT yields and an ECB lending survey showing tighter credit hit the euro harder than risk-on flows hit the yen. The cross closed near 175.60 (EUR/USD 1.1126 × USD/JPY 157.83).
eurjpy.outlook: Bearish: I lower the sell zone to 175.90–176.30 for 174.00 while euro stress and the BoJ meeting weigh. A close above 177.00 ends the call; a hawkish ECB surprise is the risk.
eurjpy.watch: The ECB (Oct 29), BoJ (Oct 30), French spreads and risk sentiment.

cnhjpy.note: Up about 0.2% to near 23.68 as the yen slipped and the yuan held firm.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. USD/JPY rose about 0.2% on the risk-on mood while the PBOC kept the yuan steady near four-year highs, so the cross edged up to about 23.68 (USD/JPY 157.83 ÷ USD/CNH 6.666).
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range, now in the upper half. A hawkish BoJ would push it toward 23.3; a break above 23.8 would need USD/JPY near 158.6.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, the BoJ on Oct 30 and risk sentiment.

watch: Next: the Fed, BoC, RBNZ and UK Budget plus Taiwan's central bank at the legislature (Oct 28), the ECB and US GDP/PCE (Oct 29), the BoJ and US tariffs on Canada (Oct 30), China PMIs (Oct 31), the RBA and US midterms (Nov 3), the BoE and Bank Negara (Nov 5), plus Iran headlines, oil, Tokyo's 159–160 line and the peso at 64.
